GK05-q01-y02xdo: Release the parking brake only after the engine gives enough power to hold the truck, and speed up smoothly.
Neutral gives no power to hold the truck; partly engage the clutch before leaving the brake.
GK05-q02-mrymhj: Braking doesn't stop wheel spin; the fix is taking your foot off the accelerator.
More power makes the drive wheels spin more; ease off the accelerator instead.
GK05-q03-5ntytl: Grip has nothing to do with power steering; a curb or pothole can jerk a loose wheel away.
A firm two-hand grip is needed whenever you drive, since a pothole can come anytime.
GK05-q04-5lbzdh: That's too early; wait until the engine has slowed to near idle.
Waiting until you've stopped is too late; clutch in near idle keeps the engine running.
GK05-q05-151q4a: Backing toward the driver's side is one of the six safe-backing rules.
Using a helper whenever possible is one of the six safe-backing rules.
GK05-q06-5o8k5x: In your path the helper could be hit; they stand near the back, where you can see them.
On the blind right side you couldn't see the helper's signals; they must stay in your view.
GK05-q07-znp9lb: Right-side backing is very risky because you can't see well; going around the block is worth it.
Speed makes blind backing worse; back slowly and toward the driver's side.
GK05-q08-bvo8y2: Turning toward the goal works for straight trucks; with a trailer you turn the opposite way.
The trailer won't steer itself; turn the wheel opposite to where you want it to go.
GK05-q09-d3dsp3: Steering away pushes the trailer further off; steer toward the drift right away.
Drift must be corrected immediately, before you get far off course.
GK05-q10-iddu0b: Synchronized manual transmissions do not need double clutching.
Double clutching is for unsynchronized manuals; with an automatic on a downgrade you pick a low range.
GK05-q11-63vqkq: Both shifts start the same way: release the accelerator, push the clutch in and shift to Neutral together.
Both shifts push the clutch in to enter the new gear — that's the second clutch in double clutching.
GK05-q12-gjzz6a: Never force it; go back to Neutral and match engine rpm to road speed first.
Staying in Neutral caused the problem; reset, raise rpm to fit road speed, and try again.
GK05-q13-fhjo1s: Progressive shifting means the shift point rises with each higher gear; it doesn't stay the same.
That's backwards: the shift rpm gets higher as you go up through the gears.
GK05-q14-oz3fyo: The climbing gear is usually too high; going down needs a lower gear to avoid hard braking.
A higher gear leaves more work for the brakes; you want a gear usually lower than the climbing gear.
GK05-q15-pbqyil: Downshifting first lets you avoid braking in the curve and use a little power through it.
Downshifting before a curve is about stability and speeding up after it, not engine temperature.
GK05-q16-n0lzwj: Neutral gives up engine braking; select a low range on a downgrade.
A high range gives little engine braking; a low range keeps it from shifting up.
GK05-q17-768ddu: On slippery roads a retarder can make the drive wheels skid; it doesn't prevent skids.
More retarder power on ice makes a drive-wheel skid more likely; turn it off.
GK05-q18-2v240m: Exhaust is one of the four basic retarder types.
Hydraulic is one of the four basic retarder types.
GK05-dn-k8pnow: 4 is the number of basic control skills; the double-clutch method has 5 steps.
6 is the number of safe-backing rules; the double-clutch method has 5 steps.
GK05-dn-go3gcu: Those are gauges to watch after start-up, not shift signals; use rpm or road speed.
Retarders and grades don't tell you when to shift up; use rpm or road speed.
GK05-dn-s9z5jm: That's too late — downshift before the hill and before the curve.
The two special downshifts are before a downhill and before a curve, not backing or lights.
GK05-dn-s9vinl: There are 4 types; this leaves out hydraulic and electric.
Air is not a retarder type; there are 4: exhaust, engine, hydraulic, electric.
GK05-dn-iwer4h: A retarder works only on the drive wheels, when you fully release the accelerator.
A retarder brakes only the drive wheels, not the trailer's.
GK05-dn-qb1xm0: A downgrade is where a retarder helps; turn it off only on wet, icy or snowy roads.
On slippery roads a retarder can make the drive wheels skid, so switch it off then.
GK05-dn-4sni4p: Back as slowly as possible, which means the lowest reverse gear.
Back in the lowest reverse gear so you can fix steering errors and stop quickly.
GK05-dn-0vcuku: The right side is your blind side, so backing that way is very risky.
Choose the driver's side even if it means driving around the block.
GK05-dn-qm2651: Direction signals help, but the one the handbook says you must agree on is "stop."
"Slow down" isn't the key one; the handbook says to agree on a signal for "stop."
GK05-dn-upl8kx: Turning toward the goal is for cars, straight trucks and buses, not trailers.
Don't wait; turn opposite first, then follow the trailer once it starts to turn.
GK05-dn-yozou5: The climbing gear is usually too high; going down needs a lower gear to avoid hard braking.
A higher gear leaves more work for the brakes; you want a gear usually lower than the climbing gear.
GK05-dn-bs8jub: Neutral gives up engine braking; select a low range on a downgrade.
A high range gives little engine braking; a low range keeps it from shifting up.
GK05-dn-s890j2: Progressive shifting means the shift rpm rises with each higher gear, not stays the same.
That's backwards: the shift rpm gets higher as you move up through the gears.
